items.summary: The economic picture on June 4 evening is defined by three threads. First: Kevin Warsh reaches Day 21 without an economic policy statement — 12 days from the June 16–17 FOMC, his inaugural meeting as Fed chair. The communication vacuum is now critical relative to the complexity of the dual-mandate environment. Cleveland Fed May nowcast 4.18% YoY; April CPI 3.8% (above 3.7% forecast); April PCE 3.3% (highest in nearly three years); Q1 GDP 1.6% second estimate confirmed. CME FedWatch: near-zero June cut probability; rate hike odds building for July and December (~40%). The Warsh silence is the primary domestic economic risk ahead of the June 16–17 window — markets have not received any signal about the chair's reaction function. Second: Bloomberg (June 3) reports that emerging-market central banks are leading a wave of interest-rate hikes as the Iran war re-ignites inflation — moving faster than developed-world peers who remain on hold to assess the fallout. The ECB and Bank of Japan are both expected to raise policy rates in June, creating a developed-market rate-convergence dynamic that adds to pressure on the Fed's relative-ease posture. The global disinflation trend is reversing under Middle East energy-price pressure; developed-economy inflation forecast rising from 2.6% to 2.9% for 2026. Third: the House Appropriations Committee marked up its FY27 Transportation, Housing and Urban Development (T-HUD) appropriations bill at $92.22 billion — a 10.4% cut from FY26 levels — with priorities skewing toward highway infrastructure, aviation, and safety over public transit and passenger rail. This is a forward-looking federal transit-deprioritization signal entering the IIJA appropriations conclusion window (September 2026). The Iran comms suspension resolution confirms the 'next week' Trump pump-relief timeline is preserved conditionally — late July at earliest if MOU signing occurs this week and 30-day mine-removal begins. Oregon gas at record $5.35/gallon; Washington approximately $5.78. Reconciliation 2.0 stuck — the anti-weaponization fund blocking provision is now characterized as generating the 'first real GOP resistance' of the session, a political stress signal that raises the probability of further delay toward the July 4 delivery deadline.

items.summary: Two major ongoing infrastructure incidents and one new regional transit signal on June 4 evening. First: the Longview Nippon Dynawave paper mill CSB investigation advances to Day 10. All 11 victims recovered and identified. Approximately 90,000 gallons of white liquor remain inside the structurally unstable tank. Columbia River contamination assessment ongoing; EPA Region 10 and WA Department of Ecology monitoring active; Longview wellhead on diversion; drinking water confirmed safe. CSB investigation in early-stage documentation — no preliminary findings published. The pre-warning regulatory thread (March 2026 workers notified WA DOLI of a sinkhole at the implosion site) defines the investigation's regulatory liability arc. Second: the Sound Transit $34.5B funding gap overhaul (board vote June 2) stands as the confirmed regional infrastructure retrenchment event. The Ballard Link Extension from Seattle Center to Market Street remains 'not currently affordable.' Revenue measures under review — fare gates, Washington Clean Fuels Standard carbon credit program, other operational changes — remain unresolved in both timeline and projected yield. The T-HUD FY27 markup (-10.4%, transit deprioritized) is an adverse federal-funding-environment signal that complicates Sound Transit's path to additional federal revenue. Third: Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson proposed renewing and expanding the Seattle Transit Measure, which would double the city's transit sales tax. This is a new development — a mayoral initiative to increase local transit revenue through a city sales tax measure, separate from Sound Transit's ST3 mechanism. The proposal introduces a new local revenue pathway but requires voter approval; timeline and ballot schedule not confirmed. Together, the Sound Transit retrenchment and the Seattle Transit Measure expansion proposal represent competing signals: regional retrenchment at ST level versus local expansion attempt at city level.

items.summary: Six local PNW threads on June 4 evening. First: Longview Nippon Dynawave paper mill CSB investigation Day 10. All 11 victims recovered. Approximately 90,000 gallons white liquor in the structurally unstable tank; Columbia River contamination assessment ongoing; drinking water safe; EPA Region 10 and WA DOE monitoring active. CSB investigation in early documentation; no preliminary findings. Pre-warning regulatory thread (March 2026 DOLI sinkhole notification) defines liability arc. Second: Sound Transit $34.5B gap overhaul (board vote June 2) remains the confirmed regional infrastructure retrenchment event. The Ballard Link Extension to Market Street is 'not currently affordable.' The additional funding mechanism — fare gates, WA Clean Fuels Standard carbon credits, other revenue — remains unresolved. New this cycle: Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson is proposing to renew and expand the Seattle Transit Measure, which would double the city's transit sales tax. This is a new local-revenue pathway attempt, distinct from Sound Transit's regional mechanism, and will require voter approval. The T-HUD FY27 markup (-10.4%, transit deprioritized) adds adverse federal-funding context. Third: the 2026 FIFA World Cup opens June 11 — 9 days from today — with Seattle (Lumen Field) hosting matches June 13 through July 7. Security and infrastructure preparation for the World Cup is active in the Seattle metro area. New Amtrak PNW trains are coming 'soon but not in time for the World Cup' (Washington State Standard) — a regional connectivity gap that will affect visitor transit options during the matches. Fourth: Blue Origin vows to fly again before the end of 2026, less than a week after the massive explosion that destroyed the New Glenn rocket — a signal of continued PNW aerospace sector ambition under acute operational setback. Fifth: Portland City Council budget T-27 to July 1 FY start. June 3 amendments session occurred; additional sessions possible. Sixth: national measles estimated at approximately 2,022–2,028, with CIDRAP slowing signal holding; school window 3 days remaining. Oregon gas at record $5.35/gallon; Washington approximately $5.78.
